hero_kpi_rationale: Net Sales remain the primary performance indicator for the company, reflecting overall commercial dynamics in a mature sector facing volume and mix challenges despite price increases.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total sales after deductions for returns and allowances.
kpis.description: Net Sales declined 3.5% in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily due to unfavorable volume/mix (-4.1 pp), partially offset by price increases (+0.7 pp).
kpis.signal: Sales decline driven by volume/mix headwinds despite price increases.

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.description: Operating Income totaled -4.7 billion USD in 2025 versus +1.7 billion USD in 2024, impacted by asset impairments (goodwill and intangible assets) totaling 9.3 billion USD.
kpis.signal: Major operating loss in 2025 due to asset impairments.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between sales and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross Margin remained stable at approximately 33.5% in 2025, supported by efficiency measures and price adjustments, despite inflationary pressures on the supply chain.
kpis.signal: Gross Margin stable despite cost inflation.

kpis.name: Impairment Losses
kpis.explanation: Amount lost on assets that declined in book value.
kpis.description: Total impairment losses of 9.3 billion USD in 2025 (6.7 billion USD on goodwill, 2.6 billion USD on intangible assets), compared to 3.6 billion USD in 2024.
kpis.signal: Massive impairments in 2025 materially affecting results.

kpis.name: Organic Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Net Sales adjusted for currency exchange effects, acquisitions, and dispositions.
kpis.description: Organic Net Sales declined 3.4% in 2025, indicating contraction in core business activity despite price increases.
kpis.signal: Organic decline reflecting weak demand or market share loss.

kpis.name: Divestitures
kpis.explanation: Proceeds received from the sale of business units or subsidiaries.
kpis.description: Divestiture of infant and specialized nutrition business in Italy for 146 million USD in December 2025.
kpis.signal: Portfolio reduction in Italy to refocus operations.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net Income extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL across the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Net Income of -5.846 billion USD in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Diluted EPS
kpis.description: Diluted EPS extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL across the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Diluted EPS of -4.93 USD in the latest fiscal year (FY2025).

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Dividend per share paid annually, aggregated from yfinance.dividends across the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend Per Share of 0.4 USD in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow across the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 1.898 billion USD in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated across the last 3 reported fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 70.4% in the latest year.

kpis.name: FD&C Colors Removal
kpis.explanation: Commitment to eliminate artificial dyes by end of 2027 in the United States.
kpis.description: Commitment announced in 2025 to remove all FD&C Colors from new products and the U.S. portfolio by end of 2027, primarily impacting Hydration and Desserts platforms.
kpis.signal: Portfolio transformation to address health-conscious consumer preferences.

kpis.name: SNAP Program Impact
kpis.explanation: Changes to U.S. food assistance program affecting demand.
kpis.description: Modifications to the SNAP program in 2025 could reduce demand for Kraft Heinz products, targeting lower-income consumers.
kpis.signal: Regulatory risk weighing on demand for affordable products.

risks.title: Intense competition and pricing pressure
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned at the beginning of the 'Industry Risks' section and is described as 'highly competitive'. The company emphasizes the need to lower prices or increase marketing spending to remain competitive, which directly impacts profitability.

risks.title: Rapid evolution of consumer preferences
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed in the 'Industry Risks' section and the company stresses the need to predict and adapt to rapid changes in consumer tastes and habits, including health and wellness trends.

risks.title: Retail consolidation and retailer bargaining power
risks.score_rationale: This risk is clearly identified in the section covering changes in the retail landscape. Consolidation among retailers gives them increased negotiating power, affecting prices and commercial terms.

risks.title: Product recall risks and liability
risks.score_rationale: This risk is presented as having a 'materially adversely affect' impact and is detailed with examples such as contamination, mislabeling, or undeclared allergens.

risks.title: Brand reputation and image damage
risks.score_rationale: This risk is central in the dedicated reputation section. It covers negative perceptions related to products, marketing practices, environmental or social issues, and rapid spread of information (including false information) on social media.

risks.title: Innovation failure and new product development shortfalls
risks.score_rationale: This risk is linked to the company's ability to innovate and introduce new products, mentioned in the section on competition and consumer preferences. Failure can impact sales and competitive position.

ai_positioning.summary: KHC does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
